mainTopic: When spoiled food and the blood mass (חררת דם) lose impurity, ביטול ברוב in brine, and רב's rule that the הלכה follows the whole פרק
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רבי ירמיה. According to רבי יוחנן, the blood mass should still be impure because a dog would eat it, and the challenge stands as a קשיא. The גמרא then returns to the original dispute. בר פדא says severe impurity lasts only while an item is fit for a גר, while רבי יוחנן says all impurity lasts until the item is unfit for a dog. Each side's reading of the פסוק about giving a נבלה to a גר is explained. Next, רבי יוחנן explains that the blood mass of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is pure because of ביטול ברוב, since it was once fit to eat as part of its mother. A related משנה about brine and water shows that עמי הארץ were suspected of mixing water into brine, and the גמרא explains why the amount is 'half'. A new משנה of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that we assume a nursing animal is nursing its own baby. רב rules that the הלכה follows this whole פרק except where there is a dispute. After testing several candidates, the גמרא concludes that this rule teaches that a dissent found only in a ברייתא does not count as a dispute. The amud ends by beginning a new challenge built on רב's general rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן, the blood mass is still fit for a dog
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge against רבי ירמיה. Under רבי יוחנן's rule, the blood mass should still be impure because a dog would eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the view that both kinds of impurity last until the item is unfit for a dog: this blood mass is fit for a dog!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge from the previous section. רבי ירמיה's explanation for why the blood mass is not impure does not fit רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that impurity lasts as long as a dog would still eat the item. A blood mass is something a dog would eat. So, by רבי יוחנן's standard, it should still carry impurity, and רבי ירמיה's reason fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one (both kinds of impurity)
Until it is no longer fit for a dog to eat

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ עַד לְכֶלֶב,
phrases.english: [According to the one who says] both this one and that one [impart impurity] until [unfit] for a dog,
phrases.notes: This is the view of רבי יוחנן, quoted below.

phrases.english: this [blood mass] is fit for a dog!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ עַד לְכֶלֶב, הָא חַזְיָא לְכֶלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun earlier against רבי ירמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's explanation of why the blood mass carries no impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי יוחנן, impurity lasts while an item is fit for a dog. A blood mass is fit for a dog, so it should be impure.

steps.title: The challenge stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The difficulty remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'קשיא', meaning the question stays open and is not resolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' is not a full rejection like 'תיובתא'. It means the challenge is strong and no answer is offered here, but the view is not formally thrown out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'קשיא' with 'תיובתא'. 'קשיא' leaves a problem unsolved. 'תיובתא' is a decisive refutation.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 1 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ירמיה's explanation remains difficult according to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: בר פדא: severe impurity until a גר, light impurity until a dog
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the original dispute. בר פדא splits the two kinds of impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: בר פדא says, severe impurity lasts until the item is unfit for a גר, and light impurity lasts until it is unfit for a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word 'גופא', the גמרא goes back to quote, in full, the argument it just relied on. It starts with בר פדא's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Severe impurity is generally explained as the impurity of a נבלה. It stops once the meat is too spoiled for a גר תושב to eat. Light impurity is generally explained as טומאת אוכלין (food impurity). It lasts longer, until even a dog would refuse it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself', which returns to a statement quoted earlier in order to discuss it
Here a גר תושב, a non-Jew living in the land, to whom a נבלה may be given

phrases.english: The matter itself: Bar Padda says:
Severe impurity [lasts] until [unfit] for a ger,
and light impurity [lasts] until [unfit] for a dog.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, בַּר פְּדָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the source of the rule used in step 1, in order to analyze it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Severe impurity ends once the item is unfit for a גר. Light impurity ends only once it is unfit for a dog.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both kinds last until a dog
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and applies the 'dog' standard to both kinds of impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן says: both this one and that one last until the item is unfit for a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the argument. רבי יוחנן uses one standard for all impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, even a נבלה stays impure as long as a dog would eat it. This is the view behind the challenge in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ עַד לְכֶלֶב.
phrases.english: Both this one and that one [last] until [unfit] for a dog.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to בר פדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both severe and light impurity last until the item is unfit for a dog.

steps.title: What is בר פדא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind בר פדא's split.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בר פדא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why בר פדא makes severe impurity end sooner. This sets up the verse that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's single standard seems simpler. So the גמרא wants to know what pushes בר פדא to give נבלה a stricter cutoff.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Bar Padda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבַר פְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for limiting severe impurity to what is fit for a גר.

steps.title: The פסוק links נבלה to what can be given to a גר
steps.stepSummary: The verse about giving a נבלה to a גר shows that only meat fit for a גר is called נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You shall not eat any carcass; give it to the גר...' What is fit for a גר is called נבלה. What is not fit for a גר is not called נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The Torah defines a נבלה as something you could give to a גר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah describes a נבלה as something fit to give a גר, meat too spoiled for a גר no longer counts as a נבלה. Once it loses that status, it loses the severe impurity of נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal carcass that died without proper שחיטה; it carries severe impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading ties a halachic status (נבלה) to the item still being usable. That idea is the basis of the whole dispute.

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כׇל נְבֵלָה לְגֵר וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: As it is written: 'You shall not eat any carcass; to the ger etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:21: 'give it to the גר who is in your gates.'

phrases.english: that which is fit for a ger is called 'carcass',
and that which is not fit for a ger
is not called 'carcass'.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לֹא תֹאכְלוּ כׇל נְבֵלָה לְגֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 14:21 defines נבלה as meat fit to give a גר. Meat unfit for a גר is not a נבלה.

steps.title: How does רבי יוחנן use this verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן learns from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יוחנן)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן deals with בר פדא's פסוק. It is setting up his reading of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק seems to limit נבלה to what a גר would eat, רבי יוחנן must explain what the פסוק teaches according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? (How does the other opinion handle this?)

phrases.english: And the other [Sage, Rabbi Yochanan]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns בר פדא's verse toward רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוחנן learns from דברים 14:21.

steps.title: The verse excludes meat that was rotten from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן uses the פסוק only for a carcass that was spoiled from the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude a case where it was rotten from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי יוחנן, the פסוק excludes only meat that was already rotten when the animal died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, meat that was edible when the animal died and spoiled later stays a נבלה as long as a dog would eat it. Only meat rotten from the start, never fit for a גר, is excluded by the פסוק.

phrases.english: To exclude where it was rotten from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי הֵיכָא דְּהִסְרִיחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק excludes only a carcass rotten from the start. A carcass that spoiled later stays impure until it is unfit for a dog.

steps.title: How does בר פדא answer that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בר פדא does not accept רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (בר פדא)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בר פדא responds to רבי יוחנן's use of the פסוק. It is setting up בר פדא's rejection of that reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק can be explained as excluding meat rotten from the start, בר פדא needs a reason why the פסוק must teach his broader rule instead.

phrases.english: And the other [Sage, Bar Padda]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יוחנן's reading back toward בר פדא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בר פדא rejects reading the פסוק as excluding only meat rotten from the start.

steps.title: No verse is needed for meat rotten from the start; it is just dust
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא says meat rotten from the start is obviously not a נבלה, so the פסוק must teach something more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat that was rotten from the start does not need a פסוק to exclude it. It is merely dust.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא rejects רבי יוחנן's reading. A פסוק is not needed to teach something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that was never edible is like dirt and plainly cannot be a נבלה. So the פסוק must be teaching a new point: even meat that spoiled later stops being a נבלה once a גר would not eat it.
steps.whatToRemember: בר פדא: a נבלה loses severe impurity once it is unfit for a גר. רבי יוחנן: it stays impure until it is unfit for a dog, and the פסוק excludes only meat rotten from the start. בר פדא answers that such meat is just dust and needs no פסוק.

phrases.english: [Where] it was rotten from the outset
no verse is needed to exclude it,
it is merely dust.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִסְרִיחָה מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא צְרִיכָא קְרָא לְמַעוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוחנן's reading from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוחנן's claim that the פסוק only excludes meat rotten from the start
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is obvious without a פסוק, because it is mere dust. So the פסוק must teach something new.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the expelled blood mass is buried and exempts from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the משנה about a large animal that expelled a blood mass.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a large animal that expelled a mass of blood: it must be buried, and the animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה again. This is setup for the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood mass may contain a fetus, so it is treated as a birth. Any later offspring therefore is not a בכור. It is buried in case it truly was a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: A large domesticated animal (e.g., a cow)
Is exempt from the law of the firstborn

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A large animal that expelled a mass of blood,
this must be buried,
and [the animal] is exempt from the firstborn status.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of discussion by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expelled blood mass is buried, and the mother is exempt from בכורה for future births.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the blood mass does not impart impurity
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that this blood mass is not impure by touching or carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא taught: it does not make things impure, neither by touch nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי חייא's teaching, which adds a law of impurity to the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising. If the blood mass may hold a fetus, we might expect it to carry the impurity of a נבלה. רבי חייא says it does not.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא.
phrases.english: It does not impart impurity, neither by contact nor by carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתָנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an impurity ruling to the case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood mass does not impart impurity through contact or carrying.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the reason is nullification in the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the blood mass is pure because of ביטול ברוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: it is because of nullification in the majority that the Sages dealt with it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the reason for רבי חייא's ruling. This sets up the coming discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any small bit of fetal flesh in the mass is outweighed by the larger amount of blood. So the whole mass is treated as blood, which is not a נבלה. That is why it carries no impurity, even though it is still buried to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullification in a majority, where a minority substance loses its identity in a larger mixture
They (the Sages) dealt with it / touched upon it

steps.confusionAlert: The blood mass is still buried and still exempts from בכורה. ביטול ברוב only removes its impurity; it does not erase the possibility that a fetus was inside.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is due to nullification in the majority that they touched upon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל בְּרוֹב נָגְעוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבי חייא's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The blood mass is pure because any fetal matter is nullified in the majority of blood.

steps.title: Why not say the blood mass was never fit to eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: why rely on ביטול ברוב, when the blood mass could be pure simply because it was never fit to eat?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did רבי יוחנן specifically say the reason is ביטול ברוב? We could learn it from the fact that the blood mass was never fit to eat at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reason from Step 13. It suggests an easier reason for why the blood mass is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the sugya there was the idea that something which was never fit to eat does not carry נבלה impurity. A shapeless blood mass was never food. So why does רבי יוחנן need the more complicated idea of ביטול ברוב?

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it instead from...

phrases.english: Why specifically because of nullification in a majority?
Let me derive it from the fact that it was not fit at all!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא מִשּׁוּם בִּיטּוּל בְּרוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבי יוחנן gave in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of ביטול ברוב for the blood mass
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reason is available: the blood mass was never fit to eat, so it should never carry נבלה impurity.

steps.title: The blood mass was once fit as part of its mother
steps.stepSummary: The blood mass was fit to eat at the start, as part of its mother. So the 'never fit' reason does not work, and ביטול ברוב is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too was fit at the start, by virtue of its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The blood mass did have a time when it was fit to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the blood mass came out, it was inside the mother. If the mother had been slaughtered then, it would have been eaten as part of her body. Because it was once fit, the 'never fit' reason does not apply, so רבי יוחנן had to use ביטול ברוב.

keyTerms.meaning: By virtue of (as part of) its mother

phrases.english: This too was fit at the start
by virtue of its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי אִיתְחֲזִי מֵעִיקָּרָא אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the item was once fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood mass was never food, so it cannot carry נבלה impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood mass was edible as part of the mother, so ביטול ברוב is the real reason it is pure.
steps.whatToRemember: The blood mass is pure because of ביטול ברוב. The 'never fit' reason fails because the blood mass was once fit as part of its mother.

steps.title: Pure brine becomes impure from any amount of water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, pure fish brine becomes impure if any amount of water falls into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, pure brine into which any amount of water fell is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that also deals with majority and nullification. It is setting up רבה בר אבוה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising: why would a tiny bit of water make pure brine impure? The case is about brine that came from an עם הארץ. The next step explains the hidden reason.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Fish brine (the liquid from salted fish)

phrases.english: We learned there:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Pure brine into which fell
any amount of water is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related discussion about nullification in a majority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure brine that any amount of water falls into becomes impure.

steps.title: עמי הארץ were suspected of mixing half water into brine
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה explains that עמי הארץ were suspected of adding half water to their brine. The extra water that falls in tips the balance and makes the mixture impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: This shows that עמי הארץ were suspected of mixing half water into the brine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר אבוה explains why any amount of water makes the brine impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water that the עם הארץ mixed in is impure, but as long as it is not the majority, it is nullified in the brine. When more water falls in, the water becomes the majority. Then its impurity 'wakes up' and makes the whole mixture impure.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are not careful about purity laws

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
This is to say
amei ha'aretz are suspected
of mixing half (water) into the brine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמי הארץ are suspected of mixing half water into brine, so added water makes the mixture impure.
steps.confusionAlert: The impurity does not come from the new water. It comes from the old water the עם הארץ already mixed in, which was nullified until the new water made the water the majority.

steps.title: Why say half? Even less than half should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבה בר אבוה said exactly half. Even with less than half, the added drop would bring the water to half, and half is not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need half? Even less than half should also work! That small amount of added water makes it half, and half is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the exact word 'half' in רבה בר אבוה's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nullification only works when one side is the majority. If the water was a bit less than half, the extra drop brings it to exactly half. Since half against half is not nullified, the mixture should already be impure. So why did he need the water to be a full half?

phrases.english: And why do I need half?
Even with less than half, also!
And this small amount makes it half,
and half is not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמָה לִי מֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the exact wording of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'half' (מחצה) in רבה בר אבוה's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Half against half is not nullified, so even less than half water plus a drop should cause impurity. The precise word 'half' seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Read it as 'up to half'
steps.stepSummary: First answer: change the reading to 'up to half', meaning slightly less than half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: up to half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer by adjusting the wording of רבה בר אבוה's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר אבוה really meant that עמי הארץ add water up to just under half. Then the extra drop brings it to half, and half is not nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to half (slightly less than half)

phrases.english: Say: up to half.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא עַד מֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: The water was slightly less than half, and the added drop makes it half.

steps.title: Both impurities are rabbinic, so they decreed only for a majority
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: both the impurity of an עם הארץ and the impurity of liquids are rabbinic. The רבנן decreed only when water is the majority, not when it is half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: the impurity of an עם הארץ is rabbinic, and the impurity of liquids is rabbinic. The רבנן decreed when water is the majority. When it is half and half, the רבנן did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer that keeps the word 'half' as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally half against half is not nullified. Here, however, the impurity rests on two rabbinic rules, so the רבנן were more lenient and made it impure only when the water is a true majority. So the water must start at a full half, and the added drop makes the water the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (an alternative answer)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
The impurity of an am ha'aretz is rabbinic,
the impurity of liquids is rabbinic.
With a majority the Sages decreed,

phrases.aramaic: בְּפַלְגָא וּפַלְגָא לָא גְּזַרוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: with half and half the Sages did not decree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא טוּמְאַת עַם הָאָרֶץ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to Step 18, as an alternative to Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Half and half is never nullified, so less than half water should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the impurity is rabbinic, the רבנן decreed only for a true majority, so the water must start at half.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for 'half': (1) read it as 'up to half'; (2) the rabbinic impurity applies only when water is the majority.

steps.title: משנה: we assume a nursing animal is nursing its own baby
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a nursing animal bought from a non-Jew is assumed to have given birth already. In a flock, we assume each mother is nursing her own baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: If someone buys a nursing animal from a non-Jew, we do not worry that it was nursing another animal's baby. If someone enters his flock and sees first-time mothers nursing and other mothers nursing, we do not worry that this one's baby went to that one, or that one's baby went to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about בכור questions. We trust that a nursing animal is nursing its own baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the bought animal is assumed to have already given birth, so its next baby is not a בכור. In the second case, we assume each first-time mother is nursing her own calf, so we know which babies are בכורות. We do not worry that babies switched mothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
Animals giving birth for the first time

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who buys a nursing animal from a gentile —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת הָיָה.
phrases.english: we are not concerned that perhaps it was the offspring of another.
If he entered among his flock
and saw the first-time mothers nursing,
and those that are not first-time mothers nursing —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ,
phrases.english: we are not concerned that perhaps this one's offspring came to that one,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ.
phrases.english: or that perhaps that one's offspring came to this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מְנִיקָה מִן הַגּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We assume a nursing animal is nursing its own offspring, both when buying from a non-Jew and within one's own flock.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule decides whether a future calf is a בכור, and which calves in a flock are בכורות.

steps.title: רב: the הלכה follows this whole פרק except disputes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: the הלכה follows every ruling in this פרק, except where the משנה records a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows our whole chapter, except where there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a general ruling from רב about the entire פרק. He says we follow the rulings of this פרק, except in places where the משנה records an argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sweeping rule covering a whole chapter at once. It gives us a default: unless we find a recorded argument, we follow what the משנה says. The next steps will ask whether this rule actually teaches anything new.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows our entire chapter,
phrases.notes: That is, the rulings stated in the משניות of this פרק.

phrases.english: except where there is a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב הִלְכְתָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ פִּירְקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה, which ended with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows all the rulings in this פרק, except where a מחלוקת is recorded.

steps.title: רב ששת: רב must have said this while dozing
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת attacks רב's rule as pointless and asks which משנה it could possibly refer to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: I say רב said this teaching while he was dozing and lying down! To which משנה does it refer?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת sharply challenges רב's rule. He says it looks like something said half-asleep, and asks which משנה it could be about. This sets up the list of candidates that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule only teaches something if there is a ruling in the פרק that is not argued with and whose הלכה we did not already know. רב ששת is about to show that no such ruling seems to exist. "Which one?" is the start of a search through the chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one? To which case does it refer?

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not mocking רב personally. "He was dozing" is a strong way of saying the statement seems to have no purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
I say that while dozing and lying down
Rav said this teaching!
To which mishna does it refer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמֵינָא כִּי נָיֵים וְשָׁכֵיב רַב אָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's rule from step 22 as having no practical use.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that the הלכה follows the whole פרק except for disputes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule like this must apply to some ruling that is not argued with and is not already known as הלכה. If no such ruling exists, the rule says nothing.

steps.title: Not the first משנה, since רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot refer to the first משנה of the פרק, because it contains a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the first משנה, but there רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first candidate, the opening משנה of the פרק, and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב himself said "except where there is a dispute." The first משנה contains an argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא, so his rule does not cover it.

keyTerms.meaning: The beginning, here the first משנה of the פרק

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the first mishna,
phrases.notes: The opening משנה of the פרק, on 19b.

phrases.english: but they argue there:
phrases.notes: The text in parentheses is the old version; the bracketed text is the corrected one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אַרֵישָׁא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering "which one?" from step 23 by testing the first candidate.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the first משנה of the פרק as the target of רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That משנה contains a מחלוקת, which רב's rule explicitly excludes.

steps.title: Not רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, since his הלכה is already known
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, because there is already a general rule that we follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב? But the teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is "a קב, but clean"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second candidate, the ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a well-known principle that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teachings are few (a small measure, a קב) but completely accurate, so the הלכה always follows him. If רב meant him, he would be telling us something we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: The teachings of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
A small measure but clean, meaning few teachings but all accurate, so the הלכה follows them

phrases.english: Rather, does it refer to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
But the teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
is "a kav, but clean"!
phrases.notes: So the הלכה already follows him, and רב's rule would add nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first candidate failed in step 24, the גמרא tests a second one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling as the target of רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule would be unnecessary, because we already follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב by general principle.

steps.title: Not רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, since a ברייתא argues with him
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule seems not to fit רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because a ברייתא records someone who disagrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? But someone argues with him in a ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling from our משנה (step 21) and seems to reject it, because a ברייתא has an opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At this point the גמרא assumes that an opinion in a ברייתא counts as a "dispute." If so, רב's exception would exclude רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Keep this step in mind, because the final answer comes back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a Tannaitic teaching that is not in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This rejection is not final. In step 29 the גמרא returns to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and accepts him as the answer.

phrases.english: Rather, does it refer to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
phrases.notes: His ruling about a nursing animal, in our משנה.

phrases.english: But someone argues with him in a baraita!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִפְלָג פְּלִיג בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second candidate failed in step 25, the גמרא tests a third one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Tentatively rejects רבן שמעון בן גמליאל as the target of רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that a dissenting ברייתא makes this a "dispute" that רב excluded.

steps.title: Not רבי יוסי בן המשולם, since רב already ruled on him
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be about רבי יוסי בן המשולם, because רב already said separately that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to רבי יוסי בן המשולם? But רב already said this once, as רב said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a fourth candidate, רבי יוסי בן המשולם in the next משנה, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had already stated directly that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם. A general chapter-wide rule would only repeat what רב said elsewhere, so this cannot be its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A Tanna whose ruling appears in the next משנה (24b)

phrases.english: Rather, does it refer to Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam?
But Rav already said this one time,
as Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם הָא אָמַר רַב חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the third candidate seemed to fail in step 26, the גמרא tests a fourth one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוסי בן המשולם as the target of רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would be a repeat, because רב already ruled explicitly on this case.

steps.title: Not the hair of a blemished בכור, since עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן argue
steps.stepSummary: רב's rule cannot be about the hair of a בכור בעל מום, because that משנה contains a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it refers to the hair of a בעל מום? But עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן argue there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a fifth and last candidate, the case of hair from a blemished בכור, and rejects it. Every option now seems to have failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה has a recorded argument between עקביא בן מהללאל and the רבנן, so רב's own exception for disputes rules it out. With all five options gone, רב ששת's challenge seems to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair of a בכור that has a blemish (discussed on 25b)
A Tanna who argues with the רבנן about that case

phrases.english: Rather, does it refer to the hair of a blemished firstborn?
But they argue there:
Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַשְּׂעַר בַּעַל מוּם מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fourth candidate failed in step 27, the גמרא tests the last one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משנה about the hair of a בעל מום as the target of רב's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That משנה contains a מחלוקת, which רב's rule excludes.

steps.title: רב meant רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a ברייתא's dissent is not a dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב meant רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. His new point is that an opposing view found only in a ברייתא does not make it a מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it refers to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and this is what רב teaches us: a ברייתא is not considered a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the candidate it rejected in step 26 and says it was the right one all along. This answers רב ששת's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא assumed that a dissenting ברייתא counts as a "dispute." רב's chapter-wide rule exists to reject that assumption: only a disagreement inside the משנה itself counts. So the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רב's rule teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, in truth (returning to an earlier option)
This is what he is teaching us
It is not considered a dispute

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule is about רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. A dissenting view that appears only in a ברייתא does not turn a משנה into a מחלוקת, so the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on the nursing animal.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's opinion is not erased. It still exists as a Tannaitic view. It simply does not count as a "dispute" that would block רב's rule, so the הלכה goes with the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle for deciding הלכה: a ruling in the משנה is not weakened just because a ברייתא disagrees with it.

phrases.english: Actually, it refers to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and this is what he teaches us:
that a baraita is not considered a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְהָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all five candidates seemed to fail (steps 24-28), the גמרא returns to the one from step 26 and overturns the reason it was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of רב's rule by rejecting a hidden assumption, namely that a ברייתא counts as a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dissent in a ברייתא makes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling a "dispute," so רב's rule seemed to have nothing to apply to.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dissent in a ברייתא is not a "dispute." רב's rule teaches that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so the rule is meaningful and רב ששת's challenge is answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, because an opposing ברייתא does not count as a מחלוקת against a משנה.

steps.title: Recalling רב's general rule to set up a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls רב's sweeping rule that the הלכה follows the whole פרק except for places with a מחלוקת. This begins a challenge to a separate, specific ruling from רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since רב said, 'The הלכה follows our whole פרק, except where there is a מחלוקת'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It reminds us that רב already gave one big rule covering the whole פרק, and the challenge built on that rule will come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's general rule says to follow the anonymous משנה everywhere in this פרק unless it records a מחלוקת. A rule that broad would seem to make any separate, case-by-case ruling from רב unnecessary. The גמרא is about to ask why such an extra statement would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And since / once it is so that. This opens an argument built on something already established.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete question by itself. It is only the first half, the 'since' part. The actual challenge ('so why did רב need to say...?') comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: And since Rav said:
phrases.notes: "Since" signals that the גמרא is building toward a challenge.

phrases.english: the halakha is in accordance with our entire chapter
phrases.notes: This means the anonymous rulings in the משניות of this פרק.

phrases.english: except for a dispute,
phrases.notes: This is the only exception, where the משנה itself records a disagreement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous step settled what רב's general chapter-wide rule refers to: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Now the גמרא uses that same general rule to question whether רב's separate, specific ruling (that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי בן המשולם) was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate, specific ruling from רב, given that he already stated a general rule for the whole פרק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the general rule already covers every case without a מחלוקת, a specific ruling for such a case would seem redundant.
